finalText:
**Merge:** Creates merge commit that ties two branches together. Preserves both branch histories — you see exactly where features came in. Non-linear history.

**Rebase:** Replays your commits on top of target branch. Rewrites your commit history. Linear, clean history. Commits look like they were made serially.

**When to rebase:**
- Local branch only — before push, clean up commit history
- Feature branch → main before merge — get linear timeline
- Staying in sync with main while developing — `git rebase main` instead of merging

**When to merge:**
- Public/shared branch — never rebase what others depend on (rewrites breaks their pulls)
- Want to preserve "this feature came from this branch" — merge commit documents that
- Integrating finished feature → main — often use merge for clear record

**Rule:** Rebase locally (what you haven't pushed yet). Merge on shared branches.

Rebase upside: clean history. Downside: loses "when did this branch diverge" info, breaks if others pulled your branch.

Merge upside: safe, documents integration point. Downside: can clutter history with many merge commits if you merge often.
